per_question.q: Which page leaves the reader more in charge of changing this?
per_question.why: In Page A, the link to the seminar sits outside the bulleted self-identification callout box, separating the reader's self-assessment from promotional redirection.

per_question.q: Which page asks less of the reader before it has earned it?
per_question.why: Page B places a promotional link to the paid seminar inside the 'identify-box' immediately after personal quotes, demanding commercial consideration before the emotional recognition has even settled.

per_question.q: Which page treats the reader as the person who does the work, rather than as someone who has to be sent somewhere?
per_question.why: Keeping the identify-box clean of commercial links in Page A lets the diagnostic exercise belong fully to the reader rather than serving as a funnel to an off-site seminar.

per_question.q: Which page gives the reader more room to decide for themselves what to do next?
per_question.why: Page A keeps the seminar link in standard body flow rather than trapping it inside the boxed reflection exercise.

per_question.q: Which page puts the author's own history to better use for the reader?
per_question.why: Both pages share identical text in the personal history section, but Page A frames the overall narrative with less immediate commercial pressure.

per_question.q: Which page makes the first screen feel more like the reader's own words?
per_question.why: The identify-box in Page A concludes purely with the resonant diagnostic observation ('Every one of them is the same forecast...') rather than terminating in a pitch link.

per_question.q: Which page's opening is easier to read straight through without being interrupted?
per_question.why: In Page B, having an external link embedded inside the identify-box disrupts the rhythm of reading the bulleted internal monologues.

per_question.q: Which page makes a reader likelier to think "that is me" in the first thirty seconds?
per_question.why: Page A allows the reader to absorb the identifying quotes and summary sentence without being diverted by an external link within the callout container.

per_question.q: Which page keeps its argument moving without a detour that breaks the thread?
per_question.why: Page B bundles all introductory metadata and ancillary callout links inside the identify-box before transitioning into the prose about the 'particular twenty minutes'.

per_question.q: Which page makes it easier to follow the line from the question at the top to the answer?
per_question.why: Page B groups the callout material tightly within the box, leaving the body text below completely uninterrupted.

A: Leaves an isolated link sitting between the identify-box and the main narrative hook paragraph.
B: Injects a commercial promotional link directly into the contemplative self-reflection box.

first_screen: Page A leaves the reader more in charge because the callout box containing the inner sentences ends with an empathetic reflection rather than a sales pitch for a seminar.
